title: Restore output parity after inference config override caused eval regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A high-severity customer reported deterministic evaluation failures (repeatable mismatches vs baseline) after a serving-side config rollout. The regression only appears for their Dedicated pool with prefix-caching enabled and for their eval harness (EvalKit v2). Investigation shows an inference-config inheritance override path caused a sampler mode to change for a subset of routes, which changed token emission around end markers and trimmed suffixes the customer relies on in their prompt post-processing.
observed_behavior: Customer's eval runs return truncated JSON blobs and occasionally append trailing punctuation, causing downstream parsers to fail. Failures correlate with model route assignment to dedicated pools and are reproducible for the customer's specific prompt set at scale.
expected_behavior: Outputs should match pre-rollout parity: stable end-marker behavior, no unexpected suffix trimming, same top-k/top-p behavior for customer routes unless explicitly changed.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer's eval harness (EvalKit v2) with their prompt fixture 'customer-fix-2026.json'
2) Target the customer's Dedicated pool 'ded-nyc-04' and route 'nlp/customer-qa'
3) Send batched requests with prefix-caching enabled and sampling_seed=42
4) Observe trailing punctuation differences and missing closing JSON braces in ~12% of responses compared to pre-rollout baseline
diagnostics: Routing logs show route config merged from template 'route-template-v3' at assignment time
Config diff: route-level 'sampling_policy: deterministic' was silently replaced by template's 'sampling-mode: hybrid' during rollout
KV cache hit rates normal; issue reproduces only when cache-hit + hybrid sampling path executed
CPU/GPU metrics stable; not a perf degradation issue
root_cause: Config inheritance merge logic in the routing layer prioritizes template fields without an explicit 'preserve' flag. During a staged rollout we unintentionally shipped a template with 'sampling-mode: hybrid' which changes the sampler state machine and the handling of end-of-sequence markers for cached prefixes, leading to altered termination behavior for affected routes.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix: revert template 'route-template-v3' to previous sampling_mode for customer-dedicated namespaces (applied 2026-03-02 02:10 UTC)
2) Temporary policy: enforce route-level overrides to explicitly preserve termination-mode until fix is deployed
3) Customer guidance: run eval with explicit 'sampling_policy' in request payload as a short-term workaround
proposed_fix: A) Update inheritance merge logic in routing service to treat sampling-related fields as 'non-overridable' unless new template explicitly declares 'allow_sampling_override = true'
B) Add unit/integration tests that exercise cache-hit + sampler transitions and verify end-marker emission parity
C) Backfill a smoke-test that runs a small customer eval fixture against any config-template changes before rollout
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix to routing service branch 'fix/inheritance-sampling-guard' (PR opened)
2) Deploy to staging and run smoke-tests including customer's eval fixture (48h)
3) Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated pools (monitor eval parity dashboard)
4) Full rollout to all regions if canary stable
5) Post-release verify: run nightly parity job for top 10 customers for 7 days
follow_up_tasks: Create an alert when parity delta > 0.5% for any customer eval run
Document sampling inheritance semantics in runtime operator guide
Coordinate with Customer Success to communicate fix and obtain sign-off from the impacted customer
Audit other templates for accidental sampling-mode changes
